rules.summary: Customer-owned cable modems and gateways are allowed only when Xfinity currently certifies the exact device for the address, speed tier, and selected services.
requirements: Check the exact model in Xfinity Device Info for the service address and speed tier.
Use a device marked for Xfinity Internet and, when applicable, Xfinity Voice.
Confirm the device is not Xfinity Prepaid equipment.
lostFeatures: Xfinity gateway-only management, security, hotspot, or automatic hardware-upgrade features may not be available.
rules.nextAction: Open Xfinity Device Info and verify the exact model before buying or activating it.

rules.summary: A customer-owned router can be used with Xfinity when the modem or gateway connection is supported and the router's ports can carry the chosen speed tier.
requirements: Keep a compatible Xfinity modem or gateway upstream.
Check the router WAN and LAN port rates against the internet tier.
lostFeatures: Xfinity gateway-only Wi-Fi management and security features do not move to a third-party router.
rules.nextAction: Check the router's WAN and LAN rates in the bottleneck finder before replacing equipment.

rules.summary: Using both a customer-owned modem and router is allowed only after the exact modem is approved for the address, tier, and services.
requirements: Verify the modem or gateway in Xfinity Device Info.
Match the modem and router port rates to the internet tier.
Use a Voice-capable approved device when Xfinity Voice is present.
lostFeatures: Xfinity gateway-only Wi-Fi management and security features may not be available.
rules.nextAction: Verify the modem first, then test the complete Ethernet path in the bottleneck finder.

rules.summary: A third-party modem or gateway does not replace the AT&T-provided gateway for AT&T Fiber service.
requirements: Keep the AT&T-provided gateway connected to the service.
rules.nextAction: Keep the AT&T gateway and evaluate a customer-owned router behind it instead.

rules.summary: A customer-owned router can operate behind the required AT&T gateway; supported BGW gateways document IP Passthrough for a downstream device.
requirements: Keep the AT&T-provided gateway in the path.
Use the gateway's documented IP Passthrough procedure when that topology is appropriate.
Check both gateway and router port rates against the internet tier.
lostFeatures: AT&T supports its gateway; third-party router administration remains the owner's responsibility.
rules.nextAction: Keep the AT&T gateway, connect the router downstream, and follow the gateway-specific IP Passthrough instructions.

rules.summary: The customer-owned router may be added, but the customer-owned modem or gateway cannot replace the required AT&T gateway.
requirements: Keep the AT&T-provided gateway and use only the customer-owned router downstream.
rules.nextAction: Change the plan to customer-owned router only and retain the AT&T gateway.

rules.summary: A third-party modem or gateway does not replace the T-Mobile Home Internet gateway.
requirements: Keep the T-Mobile gateway connected to the service.
rules.nextAction: Keep the T-Mobile gateway and evaluate a router or Wi-Fi 6 mesh system behind it.

rules.summary: A third-party router can connect to the T-Mobile gateway by Ethernet, but the gateway does not offer bridge mode.
requirements: Keep the T-Mobile gateway in the path.
Connect the third-party router to a gateway Ethernet port.
Account for the gateway's fixed routing behavior and unavailable bridge mode.
lostFeatures: Bridge mode, NAT-type changes, and gateway port-forwarding controls are not available.
rules.nextAction: Connect the router by Ethernet and choose whether to disable the gateway Wi-Fi in the T-Life app.

rules.summary: A customer-owned router may be added, but a customer-owned modem or gateway cannot replace the T-Mobile gateway.
requirements: Keep the T-Mobile gateway and use only the customer-owned router downstream.
lostFeatures: The T-Mobile gateway does not provide bridge mode.
rules.nextAction: Change the plan to customer-owned router only and retain the T-Mobile gateway.

rules.summary: A customer-owned cable modem can be used only when Spectrum currently lists the exact model as authorized for its network and the selected service tier.
requirements: Match the exact model against Spectrum's current authorized-modem page.
Confirm the modem supports the selected internet tier and service address.
Use separate Spectrum-provided equipment for any service that the retail modem does not support.
lostFeatures: Spectrum-managed Wi-Fi, hardware support, and provider router features do not move to customer-owned equipment.
rules.nextAction: Check the exact modem on Spectrum's current authorized list immediately before purchase or activation.

rules.summary: A customer-owned router can connect to the Ethernet handoff from a Spectrum modem when its WAN and LAN ports support the intended tier.
requirements: Keep an authorized Spectrum or customer-owned modem upstream.
Connect the router WAN port directly to the modem Ethernet port.
Check the router WAN and LAN rates against the internet tier.
lostFeatures: Spectrum-managed Wi-Fi and provider support for the customer-owned router are not included.
rules.nextAction: Confirm the modem handoff, then check the router's WAN and LAN rates in the bottleneck finder.

rules.summary: A customer-owned modem and router can be used together only after Spectrum authorizes the exact modem for the current service.
requirements: Verify the exact modem on Spectrum's current authorized list.
Confirm the modem supports the selected tier and service address.
Match both modem and router Ethernet rates to the internet tier.
lostFeatures: Spectrum-managed Wi-Fi, hardware support, and provider router features do not move to customer-owned equipment.
rules.nextAction: Verify the modem first, then test the modem-to-router-to-client path.

rules.summary: A customer-owned cable modem can be used only when Cox currently certifies the exact model for its network and the selected speed tier.
requirements: Match the exact model against Cox's current certified-modem list.
Confirm the model supports the selected Cox speed tier.
Confirm a used modem is no longer attached to another account.
lostFeatures: Cox limits device support to equipment rented or purchased from Cox.
Panoramic WiFi app, Advanced Security, and provider hardware-upgrade features are not included.
rules.nextAction: Verify the exact modem and tier in Cox's current certified-modem list before buying or activating it.

rules.summary: A separate customer-owned router can connect behind a Cox-compatible modem when its ports support the intended tier.
requirements: Keep a Cox-compatible modem or gateway upstream.
Connect the router WAN port to the modem Ethernet handoff.
Check the router WAN and LAN rates against the internet tier.
lostFeatures: Cox does not provide equipment support for a router obtained from another vendor.
Panoramic WiFi app and Advanced Security features are not included.
rules.nextAction: Confirm the modem is supported, then check the complete Ethernet path before replacing the router.

rules.summary: A customer-owned modem and router can be used together only after Cox certifies the exact modem for the selected speed tier.
requirements: Verify the exact modem on Cox's current certified list.
Confirm the modem supports the selected speed tier.
Match both modem and router Ethernet rates to the internet tier.
lostFeatures: Cox support for non-Cox equipment is limited.
Panoramic WiFi app, Advanced Security, and provider hardware-upgrade features are not included.
rules.nextAction: Verify the modem first, then test the modem-to-router-to-client path.

rules.summary: A retail cable or DSL modem does not replace the Verizon Optical Network Terminal that terminates Fios fiber service.
requirements: Keep the Verizon-installed ONT connected and powered.
Use the ONT's provisioned Ethernet handoff for a customer-owned router.
rules.nextAction: Keep the ONT and evaluate a customer-owned router instead of a modem.

rules.summary: A customer-owned router can use the Fios ONT's Ethernet handoff, but Verizon TV features and Verizon-managed router services can require compatible Verizon equipment.
requirements: Confirm the ONT internet handoff is provisioned over Ethernet.
Connect the customer router WAN port to that Ethernet handoff.
Keep a compatible Fios router when the selected TV service or managed feature requires it.
lostFeatures: Verizon-managed router, extender, parental-control, and support features may not apply to third-party equipment.
Non-Verizon routers cannot provide every Fios TV Home app or set-top-box function.
rules.nextAction: Confirm Ethernet handoff and TV requirements, then check the router WAN and LAN rates.

rules.summary: A customer-owned router may use the ONT Ethernet handoff, but a customer-owned modem cannot replace the Fios ONT.
requirements: Keep the Verizon ONT and change the plan to customer-owned router only.
Confirm whether Fios TV or managed features require a compatible Fios router.
lostFeatures: Some Fios TV and Verizon-managed router features may not work through third-party equipment.
rules.nextAction: Remove the modem from the proposed path and evaluate the router against the ONT Ethernet handoff.
